source_text: In interventions before the Supreme Court in the Sunita Tiwari v. Union of India case (WP (C) No. 286/2017, filed in 2017 and referred to a Constitution Bench in September 2018), representatives argued that khatna constitutes a core tenet of their faith, equivalent to male circumcision, and thus falls within the scope of constitutionally permissible religious observances rather than arbitrary customs subject to state prohibition. [5]
